area: mac4DSTEM/Core/Crystal — crystal models, CIF import, scattering factors, ACOM plan/matcher (+ their consumers in OrientationResult, AppState, ResultExport, ContentView)
summary: This area is in better shape than most: the lattice/metric-tensor construction in Crystal.swift:64-87 is a line-for-line match to py4DSTEM crystal.py:165-193, the structure-factor loop (Crystal.swift:116-135) matches crystal.py:655-690 including the `> tol` sense and the fact that f_e takes |g|² (single_atom_scatter.py:116), and `ACOMMetalParams` (OrientationMatcher.swift:329-334) is byte-for-byte identical to `ACOMParams` (Shaders/ACOMMatching.metal:4-9) with the GPU argmax tie-break matching the CPU first-max. On the ACOM convention question you asked about: the composition itself is algebraically right. `detectorBasis` (OrientationResult.swift:91-96) produces a right-handed (e1,e2,n) since e1×e2 = n, and `matrix(detectorBasis:inPlaneAngle:)` at :99-106 composes so the result's columns really are detector +x and +y expressed in crystal coordinates for a pattern rotated by +angle relative to the template — I re-derived the correlation shift (corr[m] = Σ e[a]·t[a+m], so the pattern is the template rotated by −m) and the `(na − bestBin)` negation at OrientationMatcher.swift:313-315 is correct. The residual risk in that convention is not the composition but the assumption that detector (x, y, beam) is right-handed, which nothing in Core asserts. CIFImport's refusal policy is genuinely rigorous — the metric only proposes a family, two independent generators must confirm it, "too coarsely written to tell" is separated from "does not have the symmetry", the merge tolerance is derived from written precision, and the surjectivity check at CIFImport.swift:880-894 catches the split-atom case most implementations miss. tools/ws2-crystal-test/main.swift:11-19 states its own blind spots, which is exactly the discipline this repo asks for. The defects below are concentrated in the newest (hexagonal/WS₂) surface and in what the CIF parser does when a file is incomplete rather than malformed.

findings.title: Hexagonal IPF legend labels two corners with each other's indices, and the stated green/blue key is the reverse of what the code computes
findings.why: The legend triangle puts (0,0,1) at `left`, (1,0,0) at `right`, and (cos30°,sin30°,0) at `top` (ContentView.swift:1810-1813); the label row (:1825-1831) reads "0001" / "11-20" / "10-10" left→centre→right, so the centre label describes the TOP vertex and the right label the BOTTOM-RIGHT vertex — the same left/top/right convention the cubic legend at :1779-1785 uses correctly (001 / 111 / 101). But in the crystal Cartesian frame the app actually builds (Crystal.swift:75-79, γ=120° ⇒ a1 = (a,0,0), a2 = (−a/2, a√3/2, 0)), the zone axis is a REAL-space direction (g·r_uvw = hu+kv+lw, since latInv·latRealᵀ = I at Crystal.swift:84-86). So Cartesian (1,0,0) = a1 = [100] = [2-1-10] ∈ <11-20>, and (cos30°,sin30°,0) ∝ [210] = [10-10]. The legend therefore labels the <11-20> corner "10-10" and the <10-10> corner "11-20". Independently, `HexagonalOrientationSymmetry.ipfColor` (OrientationResult.swift:471-480) sets fraction = azimuth/(π/6), green = sqrt(tilt·(1−fraction)) and blue = sqrt(tilt·fraction), so green is maximal at azimuth 0 (<11-20>) and blue at 30° (<10-10>) — the opposite of the doc comment at OrientationResult.swift:468-470 ("[10-10] green, [11-20] blue") and of the accessibility label at ContentView.swift:1836. Both errors share one root cause: treating the Cartesian x axis as the (10-10) plane normal (a*, which is at 30°) rather than the a1 direction. This is the WS₂/hexagonal path that landed 2026-08-31.
findings.failureScenario: A user runs ACOM on polycrystal_2D_WS2 with the ws2_2h model, displays IPF·Z, and reads a green grain off the on-screen key as beam ∥ <10-10>. The pixel is actually beam ∥ <11-20> — 30° away in the basal plane, the difference between the prismatic-m and a-directions. The same misreading applies to the exported acom_ipf_z PNG (ResultExport.swift:1421) and to anyone comparing the map against an EBSD/MTEX IPF.

findings.title: CIF import silently assumes P1 when a file has no symmetry-operation loop, and never reads the space-group tag that contradicts it
findings.why: `parse` only recognises symmetry from a `loop_` containing `_symmetry_equiv_pos_as_xyz` or `_space_group_symop_operation_xyz` (CIFImport.swift:216-224). If no such loop exists, the `else` branch at :300-308 takes the listed sites as "the complete cell contents (P1)" — an assertion, not a check. `_symmetry_space_group_name_H-M`, `_space_group_IT_number` and `_symmetry_Int_Tables_number` are stored into `cellValues` at :231 and then never read (grep over the file finds no reference to any of them). Nothing downstream catches it: `verifyFamily` (:753-803) tests the two family generators against whatever sites exist, and a single site at the origin trivially satisfies both, so `classifyFamily` → .cubic and `validationIssues` (CrystalModel.swift:88-104, 129-186) both pass. The repo's stated rule is that a malformed/incomplete CIF must refuse rather than guess, and here the file itself carries the statement being ignored. tools/cif-symmetry-test covers 'gold_fcc_P1' with all four sites explicit (main.swift:160-162, 698-699) but has no case pairing a non-P1 space-group name with an asymmetric-unit-only site list, so the gap is ungated.
findings.failureScenario: A gold CIF with `_symmetry_space_group_name_H-M 'F m -3 m'`, `_cell_length_a 4.0782`, and one row `Au1 Au 0 0 0 1.0` and no symop loop imports without error as a 1-atom SIMPLE CUBIC gold cell. FCC's extinction rule (h,k,l all even or all odd) disappears, so `Crystal.reflections` now emits (100), (110), (210)… and the first shell moves from (111) at 0.425 Å⁻¹ to (100) at 0.245 Å⁻¹. Every ACOM template for that phase is wrong, `KnownCrystalQCalibration`'s reference ring is wrong, and the status line reports "Imported phase model … " with no complaint. Same for `I m -3 m` iron and `F d -3 m` silicon written the same way.

findings.title: Without an accelerating voltage the ACOM templates are exactly π-periodic, so in-plane angle and Euler angles are only determined mod 180° — and nothing says so
findings.why: `planWavelength` is `acceleratingVoltage.flatMap { … }` (AppState.swift:5121-5123), i.e. nil whenever the dataset carries no voltage (set only at :2434 from the file or :3214 by hand). With nil, `OrientationPlan.project` uses curvature = 0 (OrientationPlan.swift:184) and sg = g·n. Since `Crystal.reflections` enumerates both ±hkl with identical intensity (F(−g) = conj(F(g)), so |F|² is equal — Crystal.swift:107-135) and |g·n| is even under g→−g, the spot set is exactly invariant under azim → azim+π, so every polar template is exactly π-periodic and the azimuthal correlation has two equal maxima 180° apart. The code knows this — AppState.swift:5117-5120 and OrientationPlan.swift:153-160 both spell it out. But the ACOM prerequisite list (ProductWorkflow.swift:285-302) has no voltage entry, the ACOM guidance line (:338-341) only mentions Q sampling, the success message (AppState.swift:5143) says only "Orientation plan ✓ N templates", and the exported orientation bundle records `euler_convention`, `symmetry`, `template_count` and `quantitative_status` but nothing about the excitation-error model (ResultExport.swift:519-531, fields at :551-561). A downstream reader gets φ₁/φ₂ in radians with a stated Bunge convention and no way to know they carry a 180° ambiguity. Compare DPC, which does degrade its claim when voltage is missing (ProductWorkflow.swift:325-333).
findings.failureScenario: A DM4 or HDF5 cube with no voltage metadata is opened, disks are detected, ACOM runs on WS₂ or Au. The in-plane-angle map and the φ₁/φ₂ maps are populated and exported as EMD with `quantitative_status: quantitative` (semantics.productStatus returns .quantitative for the orientation bundle whenever the Q scale is physical, ACOMWorkflow.swift:119-126). Half the pixels' reported in-plane rotation is 180° off at random (the winner is decided by float noise between two equal correlation maxima), so a grain-boundary misorientation computed from the export is wrong by up to 180° with no flag anywhere.

findings.title: A CIF loop whose value count is not a multiple of its tag count silently drops the trailing partial row instead of refusing
findings.why: `let rowCount = values.count / loopTags.count` (CIFImport.swift:203) is plain integer division with no remainder guard, and the row assembly at :206-212 indexes `values[row * loopTags.count + column]` positionally. A loop whose values do not fill whole rows is therefore truncated silently, and any row with a missing field shifts every subsequent field one column left for the rest of the loop. Many such shifts do get caught downstream by `parseNumber` throwing on a non-numeric label (:388-398), but not when every column in the loop is numeric. This is the 'must refuse, not guess' case, and the one-line `values.count % loopTags.count != 0` detector is absent.
findings.failureScenario: An atom-site loop declaring `_atom_site_fract_x/_y/_z/_occupancy/_U_iso_or_equiv` where the last row omits U_iso: the row's occupancy value is consumed as U_iso for that row and the row itself is dropped by the integer division. The imported cell is missing an atom, structure factors are wrong by that atom's contribution, and no error is raised — the same silent-multiplicity class as backlog #14 with the sign flipped, which the close-contact check at CrystalModel.swift:73-83 cannot see because a missing atom leaves no close contact.

findings.title: `radialKernelInvAngstrom` is attributed to py4DSTEM's `corr_kernel_size`, but only half that parameter is ported, with a different truncation and an unrelated fixed azimuthal blur — no DEVIATION note
findings.why: OrientationPlan.swift:69-72 and :205-210 both state that `radialKernelInvAngstrom` (default 0.08, :97) 'is py4DSTEM's corr_kernel_size'. In the reference, `corr_kernel_size` → `orientation_kernel_size` is used three ways: as the hard excitation-error cut on the TEMPLATE side (crystal_ACOM.py:778 — templates get NO radial spreading at all, they deposit into their exact shell at :807-818), and on the EXPERIMENTAL side as both a radial Gaussian σ AND a radius-scaled azimuthal σ, hard-truncated at 1σ (`sub = dqr < kernel`, :1056; the joint exponent at :1064-1082 with the azimuthal term multiplied by `radius`). mac4DSTEM instead applies the same radial Gaussian to templates and experiment (OrientationPlan.swift:218-239, reached from OrientationMatcher.swift:245-248), truncates at 3σ rather than 1σ (:219), and uses a fixed `azimBlurBins: 1.5` independent of radius (:93, :240; the matcher hard-codes 1.5 at OrientationMatcher.swift:246). There is no inline DEVIATION note on any of it, which the repo's hard rule requires for a py4DSTEM port. The numbers matter: production runs kMax = 1.2 with nRadial = 32 (AppState.swift:5125, OrientationPlan.swift:88), so radialScale = 0.0375 Å⁻¹ and sigmaBins = 0.08/0.0375 = 2.13 bins with reach 6 — each spot smears over 13 of 32 radial bins.
findings.failureScenario: For WS₂ the low-order shells are (0002) at 0.162, (0004) at 0.325 and (10-10) at 0.366 Å⁻¹. Under py4DSTEM's 1σ hard cut a (10-10) peak contributes nothing to the (0002) row (Δ = 0.204 > 0.08); under mac4DSTEM's 3σ reach it deposits exp(−0.5·(0.204/0.08)²) ≈ 0.04 of its weight there, and (0004)/(10-10) at Δ = 0.041 ≈ 0.5σ are almost fully merged. Meanwhile the fixed 1.5-bin azimuthal σ gives the r = 0.162 ring ~7× less angular smoothing than py4DSTEM's radius-scaled kernel (0.08/0.162 = 0.49 rad ≈ 9.9 bins at nAzimuthal = 128) and slightly too much at r = 0.9. A reader comparing mac4DSTEM's ACOM against py4DSTEM's, or tuning corr_kernel_size from py4DSTEM experience, gets a different template bank than the comment promises.

findings.title: The gated hexagonal IPF test pins raw Cartesian vectors and never names a crystallographic direction, so it cannot catch the legend/colour swap
findings.why: `hexKeyDirections` is `[(0,0,1), (1,0,0), (cos30°,sin30°,0)]` and `hexKeyColors` is `[red, green, blue]` (main.swift:209-211), asserted at :212-217. The test states no Miller-Bravais index anywhere, so it locks in whatever the colour function currently does and is identically green under the correct AND the swapped interpretation of which of (1,0,0) / (cos30°,sin30°,0) is <10-10>. The symmetry-invariance loop at :218-223 is also insensitive: it only checks that the colour is unchanged under the 12 operators, which holds either way. Nothing in the suite ever converts a Cartesian direction to [uvtw] and compares against the key the legend advertises — that is precisely the assertion that would have failed.
findings.failureScenario: Finding 1's swap is present in shipped code, `run-tests.sh scientific` reports 41/41 with zero FAIL lines (the 2026-08-31 W4a closeout run), and the defect reaches a user through the on-screen key and the exported IPF PNG. A mutation that swaps the green and blue expressions at OrientationResult.swift:478-479 AND the two entries of `hexKeyColors` would also stay green, because no independent statement of the convention exists to contradict either.

findings.title: Two doc comments still assert the app is cubic-only, after hexagonal symmetry and the WS₂ model shipped
findings.why: OrientationResult.swift:487-489 says '.identity is the safe fallback for future non-cubic structures until their point groups are implemented' — but `.hexagonal` is implemented three lines below (:493) and `HexagonalOrientationSymmetry` occupies :371-484. OrientationPlan.swift:16-17 says 'Current crystals are cubic, so zone axes are sampled directly in the m-3m [001]-[101]-[111] fundamental sector', while `generate` has taken a `symmetry:` parameter since :94 and Mg plus WS₂ ship as `.hexagonal` (CrystalModel.swift:256-265). The repo's rule is that no claim stands which a reader cannot reproduce.
findings.failureScenario: A session picking up hexagonal ACOM work reads OrientationPlan.swift's header, concludes the sampler is cubic-only, and either duplicates `HexagonalOrientationSymmetry.sampleFundamentalZone` or reasons about the WS₂ template bank as if it were sampled in the m-3m sector — the exact class of stale-summary error CLAUDE.md records having cost this repo three sessions already.
